name: Hungarian Parliament
places: Gyula Andrássy equestrian statue, Kossuth Square
description: The huge Gothic Revival parliament on the Danube and the square in front. Guided tours take you inside to see the Holy Crown.

name: Heroes’ Square
description: A wide square at the end of Andrássy Avenue, with a column and statues of Hungary’s founding chieftains and kings, between two art museums.

name: House of Terror
description: A museum in the former headquarters of the fascist and then communist secret police, about the people they imprisoned, tortured and killed.

name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
description: The first permanent bridge across the Danube in Budapest, opened in 1849, joining Pest to Buda below Castle Hill.

name: Dohány Street Synagogue
places: Hungarian Jewish Museum (site of Herzl’s birthplace)
description: Europe’s largest synagogue, with the Hungarian Jewish Museum next door and a Holocaust memorial garden behind.

name: Great Market Hall
description: Budapest’s largest covered market, from 1897, with produce and paprika stalls downstairs and food counters and souvenirs upstairs.

name: Liberty Bridge
places: Kermit the Frog statue, Liberty Bridge
description: A green steel bridge across the Danube, with mythical turul birds on top of its towers, leading to the Gellért Baths.

name: Budapest Operetta Theatre
description: A theatre on Nagymező Street devoted to operetta and musicals, the light-opera form Budapest is known for.

name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
places: Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial
description: Sixty pairs of iron shoes on the river bank, a memorial to the Jews shot into the Danube by Arrow Cross militiamen in 1944–45.

name: Hungarian State Opera
description: A neo-Renaissance opera house on Andrássy Avenue, opened in 1884, with a gilded auditorium. Guided tours run inside.

name: Matthias Church
description: A Gothic church on Castle Hill with a colourful tiled roof, where Hungary’s last kings were crowned. Fisherman’s Bastion is beside it.

name: Liszt Academy of Music
description: Hungary’s top music school and one of its main concert halls, in an Art Nouveau building on Liszt Ferenc Square.

name: Bartók Memorial House
description: The composer Béla Bartók’s last Budapest home, in the Buda hills, kept as a museum with his furniture, plus a small concert hall.

name: Puskás Aréna
description: Hungary’s national football stadium, opened in 2019, which also hosts big concerts.

name: Columbo statue
description: A life-size bronze statue of the TV detective Columbo and his dog, on Falk Miksa Street.
